locator.text: Display 160.3, p. 160, in the proof of Lemma C.1

evidence: paper: V(\mu, p) = \tfrac{1}{2} d_0^2 \mu^2 + O(\mu^4 p^2).

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Lean replaces the asymptotic expansion by the exact factorization V = d²μ²·Q(μp) with Q := quadraticFactor, Q(0) = 1/2, Q analytic and even. The paper's display follows in two lines: V − ½d₀²μ² = d²μ²(Q(μp) − 1/2), and Q analytic at 0 with Q'(0) = 0 (by quadraticFactor_even) gives Q(s) − 1/2 = O(s²) locally uniformly, hence the remainder is d²μ²·O(μ²p²) = O(μ⁴p²), uniformly for bounded p as the paper asserts. No declaration stating a Big-O (Asymptotics.IsBigO) remainder bound for this variance was found; the Lean needs none, because the use the paper makes of the expansion — smoothness of the signed square root of V through μ = 0 with derivative d₀/√2 — is obtained instead from the analytic objects signedRoot s = s√(Q(s)) and scaledRoot d p μ = dμ√(Q(μp)) (signedRoot_contDiff, signedRoot_hasDerivAt_zero : HasDerivAt signedRoot √(1/2) 0, scaledRoot_hasDerivAt), and from the analytic inverse solveScale (solveScale_joint_contDiff).
